**24 palavras novas** (filosofia).
**Texto do dia:** entrevista.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre filosofia da mente a partir de uma entrevista, usando cautela epistêmica e enfatizando as palavras certas.

body: Esta aula treina **ouvir e anotar informações (IELTS Listening, TOEFL Listening)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.intro: A philosopher of mind answers questions about consciousness and artificial minds.
qa: Interviewer: Can a machine be conscious?
I would be **reluctant to say** yes or no. **It seems to me** that we lack a **settled theory** of consciousness, so any verdict is **premature**.
**Not necessarily.** A system might **behave as if** it understood without there being anything it is **like** to be that system. That is the **hard problem**.
**Cautiously.** I **would not rule it out**, but I would **demand** more than fluent conversation before **attributing** an inner life.

items.q: The philosopher says machines cannot be conscious.
She thinks fluent conversation alone is insufficient evidence.
She works in a laboratory of robotics.

Exemplo

rows: **I would be reluctant to say** yes.
**It seems to me** that we lack a theory.

blocks.body: Filósofos usam **modais** (*might, would*) e **verbos de aparência** (*seem, appear*) para marcar o grau de compromisso. A ênfase recai no **verbo de hesitação**: *I’d be RELUCTANT to say*.
*Actually* e *eventually* não são “atualmente” e “eventualmente”: *Actually* = na verdade; *eventually* = por fim.

items.s: I would be ___ to say yes. (reluctant)
It ___ to me that we lack a theory. (seem)

items.ans: I would be reluctant to say

body: **Hard to pin down.** — Difícil de definir.
**Draw a blank.** — Dar um branco.
**Beg the question.** — Pressupor a conclusão.
**On balance.** — No saldo geral.
**At any rate.** — De qualquer forma.
**For what it’s worth.** — Pelo que vale.
**To a degree.** — Até certo ponto.
**Stand to reason.** — Ser lógico.
**Hedge one’s bets.** — Cobrir-se de riscos.
**Leave the door open.** — Deixar a porta aberta.
**Can a machine be conscious?** — Uma máquina pode ser consciente?
**I would be reluctant to say.** — Eu hesitaria em afirmar.
**Is fluent conversation not enough?** — Conversa fluente não basta?

items.label: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances
items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

prompts.model: It seems to me that the evidence is thin.
It behaves as if it understood, but we cannot be sure.
I would be RELUCTANT to say.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence cautious answer to the question “Can an animal feel pain?”
blocks.model: I would be reluctant to give a simple answer. It seems to me that behavior offers strong evidence. A creature may behave as if it suffered without our knowing how it feels. Yet I would not rule out genuine suffering. Prudence suggests giving animals the benefit of the doubt. That is, at any rate, my tentative view.

items.q: What does “hard problem of consciousness” mean?
items.why: **hard problem of consciousness** = problema difícil da consciência.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
